title: Battle of Debaltseve: Russia Overruns Ukrainian Salient After Minsk II
reason: Core event confirmed by multiple independent sources: Russian/separatist forces besieged and encircled Debaltseve (a Ukrainian-held road/rail salient between DPR and LPR territory) from mid-January to 18 February 2015, continuing the assault despite the Minsk II ceasefire nominally taking effect 15 February 2015 (separatist commander Zakharchenko said Minsk II didn't apply to Debaltseve); Ukrainian forces withdrew under fire to Artemivsk with casualties in the hundreds. However, two magnitude/scope details in the description do not hold up against the best-sourced figures: (1) '500 captured' is overstated — the Ukrainian General Staff's official count was 90-121 captured (with ~81-90 missing), and even the highest rebel claims cited in contemporary press were ~300, not 500; (2) calling it 'the single deadliest engagement of the 2014-2022 phase' is contradicted by mainstream sourcing — Wikipedia's Battle of Debaltseve infobox cites 179-267 Ukrainian killed (highest claim), while the Battle of Ilovaisk (August 2014) is documented with higher Ukrainian death tolls (366 per official Ukrainian military count, up to 1,000+ per a Ukrainian parliamentary commission estimate), making Ilovaisk the deadlier engagement by most citations, not Debaltseve. Country, year, and the core narrative (Minsk-II-defying encirclement and forced withdrawal) are correct; the casualty/capture magnitude and the 'deadliest' superlative are the material inaccuracies.

Missile range cited as 165-186 km, consistent with the ~160 km figure in the description. All material details (country, year, actors, secrecy motive, targets, date of first use) match precisely.

title: Russia Destroys Half of Ukraine's Power Generation Capacity in Spring–Winter Campaign
reason: Multiple independent sources confirm the campaign materially as described. IEA's "Ukraine's Energy Security and the Coming Winter" report confirms ~9 GW of generation capacity lost March-May 2024 (roughly half of winter peak demand), plus a projected 6 GW winter 2024-25 supply shortfall. Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky stating at the UN General Assembly (Sept 2024) that Russia had destroyed all Ukrainian thermal power plants and nearly all hydroelectric capacity. CNN/Bloomberg/Power Technology/Wikipedia confirm the Trypilska thermal power plant (largest in Kyiv Oblast, 1800 MW) was completely destroyed in an April 11, 2024 strike using 82 missiles/drones including Kinzhal hypersonics. UN reporting (Matthias Schmale, UN Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator in Ukraine, mid-Nov 2024) cited ~65% of Ukraine's energy production capacity destroyed. All key figures (9 GW, half capacity, 15 thermal plants, Trypilska, IEA 6GW shortfall, UN 65% figure) are corroborated by independent non-overlapping sources.

verifications.reason: Multiple independent sources confirm all material elements. Russia launched a systematic aerial campaign against Ukraine's energy infrastructure starting March 22, 2024 (nine coordinated waves through August, continuing into winter), using missiles and Shahed drones. All 15 of Ukraine's thermal power plants were damaged or destroyed by year end, per Zelensky's own statement (Kyiv Independent), with thermal's share of the energy mix collapsing from 23.5% to ~5%. Approximately 9 GW of generation capacity was destroyed — roughly half of Ukraine's ~18 GW pre-war/peak-winter capacity — corroborated by IEA and multiple outlets (Reuters/CNN citing similar figures). The Trypilska coal-fired plant near Kyiv, the largest in Kyiv Oblast supplying ~50% of Kyiv's electricity, was destroyed in an April 11, 2024 strike (confirmed by Bloomberg and CNN). Kharkiv's heating infrastructure was severely hit as part of a nationwide pattern in which 18 large CHP plants and 800+ boiler houses were damaged/destroyed. The IEA's September 2024 report "Ukraine's Energy Security and the Coming Winter" explicitly projected a 6 GW winter supply shortfall. UN humanitarian coordinator Matthias Schmale stated in November 2024 that ~65% of Ukraine's energy production capacity had been destroyed, calling the 2024-25 winter potentially the hardest of the war. Every specific figure and claim in the event description is independently corroborated.

title: Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics Declare Independence
reason: Independently corroborated: Russian-backed armed groups began seizing government buildings in Donetsk from 7 April 2014; a widely-reported sham referendum on 11 May 2014 produced a claimed ~89% vote for sovereignty (with credible reporting, e.g. from intercepted communications cited by OSW, that the figure was pre-arranged rather than counted); the Donetsk and Luhansk 'people's republics' formally declared independence on 12 May 2014 via separatist leaders Denis Pushilin and Valery Bolotov. Neither Ukraine, the US, the EU, nor Russia itself formally recognized the entities at the time, while Russia covertly supplied troops, weapons, and commanders throughout the subsequent war — all matching the description's substance, dates, and non-recognition status.

verifications.reason: Independently confirmed via multiple sources: pro-Russian armed groups began seizing government buildings in Donetsk starting 7 April 2014 (NPR, Wikipedia's "2014 pro-Russian unrest in Ukraine", France24). A referendum held 11 May 2014 produced a claimed ~89.07% vote for sovereignty in Donetsk (Wikipedia's "2014 Donbas status referendums", Time magazine), with reporting noting the figure was likely predetermined/falsified (Forbes). The Donetsk People's Republic and Luhansk People's Republic formally declared independence on 12 May 2014 (Al Jazeera, Wikipedia). Neither the US, EU, nor Russia recognized the entities at the time — Russia only recognized them nearly eight years later, on 21 February 2022, just before its full-scale invasion (Wikipedia's "International recognition of the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic"). All material details (country, year, sequence of events, non-recognition, eventual Russian backing) match the description.

title: Bakhmut Falls to Wagner Group After Nine-Month Siege
reason: Independent sources confirm: Ukrainian forces lost control of most of Bakhmut around 20 May 2023, with Wagner chief Prigozhin publicly claiming full capture that day (a "224-day operation," consistent with the fighting starting ~August 2022, i.e. ~9 months). The battle is widely described by analysts/media as one of the bloodiest since WWII. US National Security Council spokesman John Kirby stated on 1 May 2023 that Russia suffered over 100,000 casualties (20,000 killed, 80,000 wounded) on the Bakhmut front since December 2022, matching the description's casualty figure. Analysts (Kyiv Independent, US Army War College article, Al Jazeera) confirm it was Russia's most significant territorial gain since the 2022 invasion but of limited strategic value since Russian forces did not advance meaningfully beyond the city. All material details (country, year, date, actors, casualties, strategic significance) check out.

verifications.reason: Independent sources confirm all material elements: on 20 May 2023, Wagner Group chief Yevgeny Prigozhin claimed full capture of Bakhmut ('at 12 noon, Bakhmut was completely taken'); Ukrainian forces (per Zelensky) had withdrawn to more advantageous flanking positions while Russia/Wagner controlled the city center. The siege ran from August 2022 to May 2023 (~9-10 months), widely described as one of the bloodiest battles since WWII/of the 21st century. US President Biden stated at the G7 summit on 21 May 2023 that Russia had suffered 'over 100,000 casualties in Bakhmut,' matching the description's casualty figure. Bakhmut was Russia's largest territorial gain since the 2022 invasion, and is widely assessed as of limited strategic value given the cost. All country (Ukraine), year (2023), and substantive details (siege length, casualties, territorial significance) are corroborated.
